purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource (reopen a previously closed account) with scope and effect stated: account becomes active and visible with historical transactions intact. Clearly distinguished from sibling close and delete.

usage_guidelines.justification: Explicitly says an account closed with no transactions was removed and cannot be reopened, and instructs re-reading with actual_accounts_list after an error. It gives exclusions and recovery context but does not name a sibling alternative for the reopen path itself.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Goes well beyond annotations: refuses a non-account id to avoid creating an empty account, reports rather than acts when already open, and discloses that verification happens after the write so a verification-read failure is reported despite a successful reopen.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100% and the single id parameter is fully documented with a UUID pattern in the schema. The description adds the refusal semantics for a non-account id but little else about the parameter.

conciseness_structure.justification: Purpose is front-loaded and every sentence carries operational meaning, though it is dense for a single-parameter tool.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema exists, yet the description explains what gets reported and the error-state caveat. It is nearly complete, missing only a concrete description of the response shape.

summary: A strong, behaviorally rich definition that clearly states the reopen effect, the removed-vs-closed distinction, and post-write verification caveats. Only the response shape is left implicit.

purpose_clarity.justification: Clear verb plus resource and an enumerated set of updatable fields (name, offbudget, closed). Does not explicitly differentiate from sibling close, reopen, or delete, though the field list implies scope.

usage_guidelines.justification: Provides a concrete example of updating name and offbudget, giving implied usage. No explicit when-to-use-vs-alternatives guidance, especially versus actual_accounts_close for the closed field.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Annotations cover safety (non-destructive, idempotent). The description restates the updatable fields but does not disclose behavior for unknown fields, validation failures, or what the response reports.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100% and already documents id, nested fields, and length limits. The description duplicates the same field list with an example, adding marginal meaning beyond the schema.

conciseness_structure.justification: Front-loaded purpose followed by a compact field list and one example. Slightly padded by a redundant schema-shaped example but generally efficient.

contextual_completeness.justification: A reasonable update tool with no output schema and no description of the result. Adequate but leaves error behavior and response undocumented.

summary: Adequate but conventional: clear fields and an example, yet no guidance on close-vs-update, no error behavior, and no response description. The schema does most of the work.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource and scope: runs third-party bank sync (GoCardless, SimpleFIN) for one linked account or all linked open accounts. Scope from omitting accountId is explicit.

usage_guidelines.justification: States the refusal conditions (local, closed, half-linked, unknown, or no linked account) and advises re-listing transactions before retry after a timeout. Strong guidance, though no sibling alternative is named.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Excellent disclosure beyond annotations: detailed return shape with count/ids and truncation up to 100 ids, never-retried semantics, timeout may still import, and the session-buffer caveat about when other clients see imports.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100% and the schema already says omitting accountId syncs all linked accounts. The description restates omission semantics without adding new parameter detail.

conciseness_structure.justification: Long but dense, with purpose first and each sentence carrying operational weight. No wasted filler.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema, but the description fully documents the return shape, truncation, timeout behavior, and partial-failure visibility. Complete for this complexity.

summary: An exemplary definition: explicit scope, refusal conditions, response shape with truncation, and nuanced failure and visibility caveats. Only the parameter coverage overlaps the schema.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource and scale: sets budget amounts and/or carryover for many month/category pairs in one call, with the 1-to-100 bound and per-operation minimum stated.

usage_guidelines.justification: Explains retry caution after timeout, directs reading the month with actual_budgets_getMonth before retry, and outlines the rebalance workflow. Strong, though alternatives like the single setAmount tool are not named.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Discloses non-atomic application with no rollback, partial failures per item, the amount-applied-before-carryover-failure case, last-wins on duplicate pairs, the full return shape, and that all-fail is a normal result.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100%, but the description adds meaning beyond the schema, notably that each operation needs at least one of amount or carryover, amount is integer cents, and duplicate month/category last-wins.

conciseness_structure.justification: Organized with behavior, return shape, guidance, and an example. Long but every block is useful.

contextual_completeness.justification: Despite no output schema, the return object is fully described and all edge behaviors are covered. Complete and self-sufficient.

summary: Very strong batch definition that thoroughly explains non-atomic semantics, partial-failure reporting, and edge cases, plus a documented return shape. Guidance is excellent though it omits named alternatives.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource: exports the active budget as an Actual Budget zip written to the server export directory. States the returned path, size, and sha256 rather than contents.

usage_guidelines.justification: Explicitly recommends using it before bulk or destructive changes as a backup and notes restore via actual_budgets_import. Clear context without a when-not condition.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Adds meaningful context beyond annotations: written to a server path, not inlined because exports are megabytes of binary, downloadable by the server operator. Does not address overwrite behavior for an existing filename.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100% and the schema documents the optional filename, no directory part, timestamped default, and appended zip suffix. The description largely duplicates this via examples.

conciseness_structure.justification: Front-loaded purpose with two brief examples. The examples are somewhat redundant with the schema but clarify invocation.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema, but the return fields are named. Behavior around file location and non-inlining is covered; overwrite handling is not.

summary: A clear export definition with good rationale for writing to the server and naming return fields. Minor duplication with schema and no overwrite behavior, but solid overall.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource and scope: gets budget data for a specific month and returns categories with budgeted, actual spending, and available balances. Month specificity differentiates it from getMonths.

usage_guidelines.justification: Points to actual_budgets_getMonths for available months, giving implied usage. No explicit when-to-use-versus-getMonths or get_all guidance.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Annotations declare a safe read. The description meaningfully describes the return content (budgeted amounts, actual spending, available balances per category), which is real value beyond the hints.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100% and the schema already documents the YYYY-MM format and points to getMonths. The description repeats the format without adding parameter meaning.

conciseness_structure.justification: Two tight sentences, purpose first. Concise and clear, though nearly all content is the purpose line plus return summary.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema; the description names the main returned fields but not their structure. Adequate for a simple read, with a modest gap in response detail.

summary: An adequate read definition: clear month scope and a useful summary of returned fields, but weak usage guidance and reliance on the schema for parameter meaning.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource: lists all available budget months with summary data (total budgeted, spent, income). Distinguishes itself from the single-month getMonth sibling by listing all.

usage_guidelines.justification: Says it is useful for viewing budget history and trends, which implies usage. No explicit when-not or sibling alternative comparison.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Annotations declare a safe read; the description adds value by describing the return array contents (budgeted, spent, income per month), which the annotations do not cover.

parameter_semantics.justification: Zero parameters, so the baseline is 4. There are no parameter semantics to explain and the schema is trivially complete.

conciseness_structure.justification: Three compact sentences with purpose first. No filler, though the trend sentence borders on generic advice.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema, but the description names the per-month summary fields. Adequate for a simple no-param list; entry structure beyond those fields is assumed.

summary: A clean, simple list definition with useful return-field context. Usage guidance is thin but acceptable for a no-parameter read tool.

purpose_clarity.justification: Despite the ambiguous name, the description clarifies the concrete action: get the budget files on the server that this session may use. Scope is explicit.

usage_guidelines.justification: Says it is useful for multi-budget management and discovering available budgets, implying usage. No explicit when-not or comparison to list_available or switch.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Annotations declare a safe read; the description adds scope nuance by saying only budgets this session may use are returned, which is real context beyond the hints.

parameter_semantics.justification: Zero parameters, so the baseline is 4. There is nothing else the description needs to convey about parameters.

conciseness_structure.justification: Two short sentences, front-loaded. Efficient with no waste.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema and the description does not say what a budget file entry contains (id, name, active state). Adequate purpose statement but leaves the return shape undocumented.

summary: Clear enough for a simple no-parameter list, with useful permission-scope context. Weakest in return-shape detail and lack of contrast with list_available or switch.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource and scope: holds an amount from this month's budget to carry into next month, with the important clarification that it operates on the month as a whole, not a category.

usage_guidelines.justification: Strong operational guidance: re-read the month before retrying after an error and warns that blind retry double-holds because Actual adds to the buffer. No named sibling alternative, keeping it at 4.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Discloses clamp-to-remaining behavior, possibility of holding nothing, partial-hold flagging, that the response reports the actually-held amount, and the after-write verification caveat. Deeply informative beyond annotations.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100%, but the description adds meaning beyond the schema by stating the amount is in cents and that the operation applies to the month as a whole, not a category.

conciseness_structure.justification: Well organized with purpose, behavior, a scope note, and error guidance. Long but each part earns its place.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema, but behavior, clamping, partial reporting, and retry dangers are all covered. Complete and self-sufficient.

summary: A rich, well-structured definition that explains clamping, partial holds, additive buffer semantics, and verification caveats. Only the lack of named alternatives keeps usage below top.

purpose_clarity.justification: Specific verb plus resource and accepted formats: restore or import from an Actual zip export or YNAB4/YNAB5. The destructive nature and effect on the active budget are stated clearly.

usage_guidelines.justification: Explicit when-not (never call to have a look), a requirement to confirm before overwriting real data, exactly-one-of path or base64, and a recovery workflow using list_available and switch.

behavioral_transparency.justification: Excellent disclosure beyond annotations: budget id comes from the archive so re-import replaces the local copy, result uploads as a new budget file, and the import loads the budget so the session's active budget changes.

parameter_semantics.justification: Schema coverage is 100%, but the description adds important semantics not enforced by the schema: exactly one of path or base64, and filename used only with base64. Strong value over the schema.

conciseness_structure.justification: Front-loaded purpose with bolded destructive warning, then behavior, guidance, and two controlled examples. Long but organized and useful.

contextual_completeness.justification: No output schema, but the destructive effects, format options, active-budget side effect, and recovery path are all documented. Complete for a complex destructive tool.

summary: An excellent destructive-tool definition: explicit replacement semantics, active-budget side effect, confirmation guidance, and exactly-one-of input rule. Thorough and well organized.
